desc:
A rectangle is divided into unit squares. Each square either is empty or has one diagonal line drawn through it, from corner to corner. The array cells describes the squares row by row:

  • 0 — empty square, no line;
  • 1 — a line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner (like /);
  • 2 — a line from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner (like \).

The lines cut the rectangle into regions. Return the number of regions.

cells = [[0,1],
         [1,0]]   -> 2
cells = [[1,2],
         [2,1]]   -> 5

In the first example the two / lines join at the middle point and form one straight line from the top-right corner to the bottom-left corner of the 2 × 2 rectangle, which cuts it into 2 regions. In the second example the four lines form a diamond: 1 region inside the diamond and 4 corner triangles outside, 5 regions in total.
constraints: A line never leaves its own square
hints: A diagonal line is hard to represent on a grid of squares. Can you make the picture finer so that a line becomes a set of blocked cells?
Blow every square up to a 3 × 3 block of small cells. An empty square becomes 9 free cells; a / square blocks the anti-diagonal of its block; a \ square blocks the main diagonal.
Now count the connected groups of free small cells with a flood fill. Each group is one region.
editorial: Upscale the picture by a factor of three. For a square at (r, c) the small block covers rows 3r..3r+2 and columns 3c..3c+2. A / blocks the small cells (0,2), (1,1), (2,0) of the block and a \ blocks (0,0), (1,1), (2,2). The lines of neighbouring squares meet exactly at the shared corners, so they remain connected in the finer grid, while the free triangles on both sides of a line stay separated (the diagonal cells are blocked and there is no way to step across a diagonal with four-directional moves).

The number of regions of the original picture equals the number of 4-connected groups of free cells in the (3R) × (3C) grid. Count them with a flood fill and an explicit stack. The grid has at most 120 × 120 small cells, so the time is O(R · C) with a constant of 9. Another well-known solution uses union-find with four triangles per square.
